name: Terminal Settings Surface
description: Owns the Settings dialog over the Workbench, closed by its close button, Escape or a press on its scrim: a navigation column with search and eight categories (General, Appearance, Themes, Terminal, Notifications, Keyboard, Agents, About) and a centered column of grouped cards whose rows each carry a name, an always-visible description and one immediately applied control. It covers System, English or Simplified-Chinese display language, application and terminal appearance, Light and Dark theme groups whose Choose theme button opens a quick pick over the window that previews the highlighted theme on the whole window, copy-on-select, the new terminal folder, terminal history, macOS Option-as-Alt, shell launch profiles, notifications, keyboard shortcuts, restore-after-restart choices, and About with the window's version and Check for updates, with per-setting restore default, a per-row reason when the settings file refuses a change, a read-only page while the file cannot be parsed or read, dismissible page notices, global search and the settings file's real path for the options the page leaves out, without unmounting the Workbench or projected terminal attachments.

states: Inspect the light English dialog: its close button, search and the seven categories with line icons in the navigation column, the filled selected category, and the centered column with the category title, an unnamed card for the language row, the After a restart group and the config.toml row with its copy action.

Change Language to Simplified Chinese and back to verify immediate mounted-copy replacement, the changed dot and the Restore default action. Type in search to see matches grouped under category names and the plain empty state, and press Escape to clear the search before Escape returns to the workbench.

Inspect the App appearance, Terminal colors and Terminal text groups. Choose Custom terminal colors to reveal the text and background color rows, and enter an out-of-range font size to see the row error while the applied size stays. Open the font list to see the fixed-width families in their own faces, switch on Show all fonts to see the other fonts with the picture fonts named in the normal face, and type a name the list lacks to see its Use entry; step the size with minus and plus. The terminal preview under the Font row follows the highlighted font while the list is open, and every size step.

Inspect the settings file with a syntax error: one notice above the title names the file path, line and column and cannot be dismissed, the rows show the last valid values with read-only controls, and no Restore default action appears.

Inspect the Light theme and Dark theme groups: the theme each slot holds, the In use now tag on the group in use, the one-line note on the other group when the app appearance is fixed, and a Choose theme button on each. The terminal preview above the groups shows the committed theme.
The Themes page with the app appearance Light: each group names its theme beside a Choose theme button, and the window stays light while no list is open.
The Themes page with the app appearance Dark: the window stays dark while no list is open, and each group names its theme beside a Choose theme button.

The Light theme quick pick over the window with the current light theme highlighted and the search field ready; moving the highlight previews its theme on the whole window, Enter keeps it, and Escape or a press outside restores the previous presentation and reopens Settings at the Light theme button.
The Dark theme quick pick over the window with the current dark theme highlighted; the same preview, keep, and restore behavior as the Light list.

Inspect Selection and keys with copy on select and the macOS Option-as-Alt row, Output with the new terminal folder select and terminal history in megabytes with their new-terminals notes, and the Launch profiles card: Default label or Use as default per profile, inline editing that saves on Done, Add profile, and the confirmed restore of the default catalog.
Inspect When to notify with the Agent notification and completion reminder choices, and Sound and delivery with the sound switch.

Inspect the long-list card: the filter row with search, Record keys and the shown count, one shortcut per line with its recorder, custom bindings with the changed dot and Restore default, and conflict notes in the row.
Inspect the Agents category: the resume-on-restore switch with its description, and nothing else.

Inspect About last in the navigation with its info icon: one unnamed card with Version showing 1.3.0 and Release build, and Updates with the hourly-check description and Check for updates. Press it to see Checking… replace the action without moving the row, then Orchbee is up to date in the positive tone. Search for a word from About to see that it lists nothing from it.
Inspect the disabled, spinner-free Checking… action over the unchanged description.
Inspect Orchbee is up to date in the positive tone with Check for updates available again.
Inspect the failure sentence in the danger tone with Get installer beside Check for updates to install from orchbee.com or try again.

Inspect a Session whose handshake lacks the request: Check for updates disabled, Get installer beside it, and the description Available once the Session updates. Or install from orchbee.com—terminals and Agents keep running.
Inspect a newer version offered: the footer's Update in the place of Check for updates, and the Update tooltip's sentence as the description.
Inspect Simplified Chinese copy in the dark appearance: unclipped navigation labels, two-line descriptions at most, and controls on one vertical line.
Inspect retained Custom terminal colors with the text and background rows shown and changed dots on the modified settings.
Inspect the localized theme groups with the dark group in use, the note on the light group, and the Choose theme buttons.
Inspect localized terminal behavior groups and launch profiles without login-shell support.
Inspect localized notification groups.
Inspect the localized shortcut list with Standard-platform key labels.
Inspect the localized resume-on-restore switch.
Inspect localized About in the dark appearance: 关于 last in the navigation, 版本 with 正式版, and 更新 with 检查更新 on the control column.
Inspect the localized Checking… action.
Inspect the localized up-to-date sentence.
Inspect the localized failure sentence with 下载安装包 beside 检查更新.
Inspect the localized Session reason with the disabled action.
Inspect the localized Update control and its sentence.

useWhen: A user explicitly chooses English or Simplified Chinese after automatic system or Browser locale resolution.
A client changes local Orchbee appearance, the Light or Dark color theme, terminal font and size, copy-on-select, or effective default terminal colors.
A user searches all available Settings categories and rows without first knowing their owning category.
A client searches, records-to-find, reviews, or changes one of the frequent Workbench or focused-terminal shortcuts.
A macOS Desktop client chooses whether the left, right, both, or neither Option key acts as terminal Alt.
A Desktop client creates, edits, selects, or removes the Session's shared system-shell and custom-executable launch profiles for future terminals.
A Desktop client changes the terminal history default captured only by future terminals.
A user wants to configure Agent notifications, completion reminders, or notification sound.
A user wants to see which version and build the window runs, or ask the Session to check for updates now.
avoidWhen: A native window, operating-system transparency, palette, VT, or OSC setting is being configured.
An option is rare or advanced; it stays in config.toml and the page only points there.
invariants: Opening Settings shows one large dialog over the Workbench on a scrim: the Workbench and projected terminal attachments stay mounted and inert, and the close button or a press on the scrim returns exactly where the user was. Escape clears a non-empty search first and otherwise returns, unless a control consumes it. Below the medium breakpoint the navigation stacks above the content.

Each category shows its title, then groups of a small muted heading and one card; a category with three or fewer settings may use one unnamed card. Each row carries a name, an always-visible description of at most two lines, and exactly one control aligned to the row's end; only the new terminal folder row adds its folder field under its select, while that select shows Custom folder….

Every change is one edit of the settings file and shows once the file answers; the page has no Save, Discard, or footer. A setting the file sets shows a dot after its name and a Restore default action that removes only that key. A refused change leaves the control at the file's value with one short reason under the row.

While the settings file has a syntax error or cannot be read, the page shows the last valid values with read-only controls and one notice naming the file path, with line and column for a syntax error.
Long lists are one card with one entry per line, and a list of more than eight entries shows a filter box with the shown count.
Search filters every available category by setting name and description, groups matches under category names, and shows a plain empty state; it changes no preference.
A page-wide notice is a dismissible banner above the category title; dismissal hides it for the open page only.
Text and background color rows appear only while terminal colors is set to Custom.

A language the file does not set uses ordered system or Browser locale resolution without writing a default; either explicit language selection persists and immediately takes precedence for mounted product copy, while user data and existing shared titles remain unchanged.

Application theme, terminal display theme, overlays, cursor presentation, and every mounted projected terminal publish through one exact Host-theme-revision barrier; data-theme changes only after all participants synchronously commit.

Choose theme closes Settings and shows one quick pick over the window that holds the themes of its polarity by name, with a search field always shown and a check on the slot's effective theme; the group in use carries an In use now tag and, when the app appearance is fixed, the other group carries a one-line note. Moving the highlight, by keys or pointer, previews the theme on the application and every mounted terminal without saving; Enter or a click stores it in its polarity's slot and leaves the app appearance alone, so the window shows the theme the app appearance selects; Escape or a press outside restores the committed theme and reopens Settings at the group's Choose theme button, and a refused save restores the committed theme. While the list is up the Workbench behind it stays inert, so a press over a Panel only closes the list.
Font family, size, and copy-on-select update mounted projected terminals without replacing their attachments.

The font row is a field that takes a font list, committed on Enter or when it loses focus; Escape takes back an uncommitted edit, an empty field restores the default, and a list that does not parse or is over 256 UTF-8 bytes shows the invalid notice and neither previews nor saves. Browse opens the searchable list of installed families from the composition's font catalog, fixed-width families first and alone until Show all fonts is on, each named in its own face except picture fonts; a search looks through every family and also offers the typed text. Picking a family moves it to the front of the field's list and keeps the rest, and the built-in entry restores the default. Without a catalog the list holds the built-in entry and the typed text. Font size is a minus, value, plus stepper that applies each step at once.

Font size precedes Font, whose row carries a terminal preview across its width, and the Themes page starts with the same preview: a prompt, a listing and the sixteen ANSI colors in the candidate font, size and colors, meaning the highlighted font, a valid typed font list, a valid typed size and the presented theme, else the committed values, resolved as the window paints its terminals. A preview never writes, and search hides it.

Shortcut edits publish one complete conflict-free effective table; Action availability is resolved before an event is consumed. Shortcut discovery filters localized visible text, stable identifiers and current chord aliases; Record keys compares one captured canonical chord exactly and never edits or persists a binding.
Recording, resetting, and restoring shortcut overrides never remount Workbench or replace a projected terminal attachment.
Option-as-Alt defaults to off, lives in the settings file, resolves the selected physical Option side per key event, and updates every mounted projected terminal without replacing its attachment.

Desktop shell profiles live in the settings file under the Server platform's keys, change only executable and literal ordered arguments, and affect only terminals launched after the Server commits the catalog; running and restored terminals retain their captured launch.

Terminal history commits to the settings file, and the Worker gives it to each terminal it launches after the save, so existing history never changes; a composition without that control omits the Output group.

The new terminal folder row offers Workspace folder, Home folder, Same as the current terminal and Custom folder… in the TUI's order and words, stores `workspace`, `home`, `follow` or the folder in `terminal.new_cwd`, shows unset, empty and `follow` as Same as the current terminal and any other text, `current` included, as Custom folder… with its text, and says it applies to terminals the orchbee command creates. Custom folder… asks the composition's folder picker when it has one and otherwise opens the folder field; a cancelled picker keeps the stored value.
The surface never reads or edits a shell startup file, executes a source command, or requests notification permission except from the notification banner's Allow button.
The config.toml row shows the path of the settings file the Session reads, from its snapshot, with a copy action; the page opens no file and adds no native capability.

No current composition runs a Host-owned terminal-theme transaction: a Desktop window, as a Server Client, paints default-coded cells through defaultColorOverride, with the selected color theme's canvas for Theme and Host and the custom pair for Custom. Explicit colors, palette projection, cursor, VT, and OSC state retain their Host authority.

About is the last category and holds no setting: no settings-file line, and search never lists it. Version shows the version the window runs with its build; Updates shows Check for updates, a disabled spinner-free Checking… while a run is queued or running, Get installer beside Check for updates when a check fails or the Session cannot check, and the composition supplies an external browser port, or, while a newer version is offered, the footer's Update Action with its tooltip sentence. Check sends workbench.update-check only when the build is not a development build, Main can offer the window a newer version, and the Session's negotiated capabilities list update-check; otherwise it is disabled with that reason. A finished result shows only for a check this window started; an installed version shows as the offer and never as Up to date; a refused, lost, or late answer, or one of another kind or for another request, fails the check and is never repeated.
All product copy ships in English and Simplified Chinese.
Navigation and search project only categories and settings whose required composition capabilities are present; roadmap-only categories and controls remain absent.
